report:
Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. PASS for the scoped new104 reductions. The packet establishes the stated equivalences and conditional sufficient criteria; it constructs neither arbitrary-current density nor a counterexample to original P21.3. No substantive repair is required.

I checked the new proofs independently and opened the matching primary statements and pertinent proof bodies. The scoped103 grant is used only for its stated ordinary middle-cone multiplication and compatible-current closures. Its supplied PASS report is not an independent justification for any new inference. The passage indexed −1 records this task-granted support, which is excluded from the external premises list.

Lemma 1 is correct, including pairings with a kernel. A finite basic neighborhood disjoint from A places the evaluation vector outside the closure of its finite-dimensional image. That closure is a nonempty closed convex cone. The nearest-point argument gives a=z−t with a·z=0, a·y≥0 on the cone, and a·t=−||t−z||²<0. The resulting separator is a finite linear combination of the original testing functionals. No infinite-dimensional separation theorem or completeness assumption is needed.

Theorem 2 is correct. The continuous diagonal involution J gives Π=(1+J)/2; symmetric currents pair through Π. Continuous functionals on the symmetric test space extend through this projection, so the dual used here consists of ordinary continuous currents. For bidegree (p,p), the tests detecting d′T and d″T have respective degrees (q−1,q) and (q,q−1). Their differential images both lie in (q,q). Taking either input to be zero shows that annihilating B imposes each closedness equation separately. These degrees remain valid at p=0 and p=n−1. Applying Lemma 1 to P+B produces a continuous ordinary symmetric current; nonnegativity on P and annihilation of ±B then establish positivity and both closedness equations. Thus H=C* in the specified pairing. No algebraic dual of a moment image is substituted.

Theorem 3 is correct for a convex construction cone containing zero. Finite feasibility requires one actual member of G on the entire fixed N, already exactly positive and doubly closed. After that existence assumption, finite test sets and increasing integers form a directed indexing set, and the selected currents converge against every test. Finite constraints are never used to certify an otherwise unverified chart functional. Lemma 1 gives the individual polar criterion, and Theorem 2 gives C⊆closure(G) exactly when G*=H. The reverse inclusion closure(G)⊆C follows directly from the positive-test inequalities and differential annihilations. Compact localization expresses each test using finitely many moment presentations; directing over all tests retains every further refinement. It supplies no construction of the required candidates. For the version of the generated cone already closed under actual weak positive limits, exhaustion is correspondingly equivalent to membership in that cone.

Corollary 3.1 has its stated conditional force. The neighborhoods must lie inside each particular open carrying the pair. A conclusion known only on one fixed neighborhood does not establish the every-open antecedent. The scoped103 grant makes the constructed approximants compatible. Its potentially discontinuous differentiating factor is correctly oriented against the continuous U or V, with positive inner currents and the restriction p≤n−2. Compatible gluing requires agreement on overlaps, and smooth decorations retain the output-degree bound.

The multiplier convergence needed in Corollary 3.1 is established for nets. On a fixed symmetric test decomposition, weak convergence gives an eventual bound on the tested positive masses. A compact cutoff followed by smooth scalar density approximates h on the full support of the sum of the positive tests. For a fixed smooth approximation, multiplication converts evaluation into evaluation on another ordinary compact smooth test. The two approximation errors are bounded by their respective tested masses. This proves convergence for the signed continuous multiplier without asserting positivity of hT or passing a discontinuous multiplier through a varying-current limit. Differential continuity and the ordinary current sheaf then give the conditional equality.

Lemma 4 is correct. The coefficient-measure bound gives finiteness, the stated upper bound, and the Lipschitz estimate after taking suprema over the same normalized family. A current with zero tested mass has zero pairing by that bound. Only a strictly positive tested mass is divided into the current. Consequently vanishing of the normalized supremum is equivalent to vanishing of all unnormalized pairings; neither total-mass normalization nor compactness of the normalized current family is required.

Theorem 5 is correct. The bound c=||g|| on Kη makes cη±gβ positive because the coefficients of η1 and η2 are c±g and c∓g wherever those forms are nonzero. The two H-memberships are, by Theorem 2, precisely |L_g(T)|≤a⟨T,η⟩ for every T∈C. Positive-mass scaling and the zero-mass estimate identify the infimum with Λη(g;α). The admissible set is a nonempty closed upper ray. Lemma 4 gives the approximation error at most ε_j, provided approximation holds on all of Kη, as required here. The relation DJ=JD makes D(hT) symmetric, so symmetric tests detect its vanishing. The numerical normalization can depend on the decomposition, while its zero condition cannot.

Corollary 5.1 is correct. Each certificate is an equality of actual compact ordinary forms. Evaluation on a positive doubly closed current eliminates both first-exact terms and gives the two scalar inequalities. The resulting error is at most (a_j+||g_j−h|| on Kη)⟨T,η⟩, which tends to zero for each fixed current. H-membership suffices by the established bipolar identity. Certificate existence is not inferred from canonical Hessian nullity.

A harmless notation clarification covers the empty-support case: use ||h|| on the empty set equal to zero. If η=0, then β=0, and both Λ and the scalar infimum are zero. This requires no new argument.

The ordinary-calculus hypotheses apply on the original opens over complete fields with either valuation regime. Compact-support localization requires no global paracompactness. No smoothness, reducedness, component classification, scalar extension, or replacement calibration is introduced. The integration comparison retains actual generic component lengths. The proofs do not need the erroneous dimension-equality clause attached to CLD's compact-moment statement. The selected supporting calculus and its applicability were checked in [CLD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2).

The literature scope checks are accurate and remain diagnostic. [CLD §1.6.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2#page=38) convolves distribution coefficients on a real vector space; it supplies no analytic-neighborhood current construction. [GR v2 §1.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.13548v2#S1.SS2) gives the generated-to-classical direction, while [§4](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.13548v2#S4) retains both nontrivial valuation and already real-PL hypotheses; its proof uses residual nefness, base extension and curve tests. The inspected [toric v1 preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.07392v1) has the 15 February 2021 header. Its regularization concerns functions on NΣ, its §4 arbitrary-current factor is Lagerberg and assumes a smooth fan, and its non-Archimedean comparison concerns toric metrics and constructed Chern products. These inspected units are not automatically identified with the 2025 publication. [Jell v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.0676v3#page=19) concerns smooth first-differential kernels and local exactness; it does not regularize arbitrary currents or continuous zero-Hessian functions. The investigation is selected, and no exhaustive nonexistence conclusion is needed or supported.

Finally, canonical equality tests only the seed δX. It does not establish G*=H, the scalar vanishing criterion, certificate existence, or two-sign generated-Psh membership. An exhaustion separator need not be a detecting functional arising from an admissible equal-curvature pair. The packet correctly leaves those geometric antecedents unproved and original P21.3 unresolved.

passages.statement: CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, §§11.1, 11.1.7, 15.2.2–9 and 15.7.1–2: Over a complete non-Archimedean field, possibly trivially valued, analytic spaces have compact-neighborhood bases and ordinary opens are analytic domains. A topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space has a canonical calibrated level-n tropical structure compatible with analytic-domain restriction. A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically and differentially separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space, compact sets admit compact smooth cutoffs inside prescribed ordinary neighborhoods; compact continuous real scalars admit uniform compact smooth approximation inside prescribed neighborhoods of their supports; and ordinary covers of compact sets admit finite nonnegative compact smooth localization summing to one nearby.

CLD v2, §§1.1.2, 6.4.6 and 7.1.1–7: On a level-n tropical space, currents of bidegree (p,p) are continuous linear functionals on compact ordinary smooth (n−p,n−p) tests, with weak topology given by pointwise testing. J is continuous and is an involution in diagonal degrees; symmetric currents are its fixed points. On a locally differentially separated space, currents form an ordinary sheaf, and restriction uses continuous extension of compact tests by zero.

CLD v2, Proposition 6.5.2 and §§7.2.1–4: A compact symmetric smooth diagonal form supported in a paracompact locally differentially separated open is a difference of two compact middle-positive smooth forms. The support condition holds on good Hausdorff analytic spaces. Middle-positive currents are symmetric and nonnegative on middle-positive complementary compact tests; their cone is convex, pointed, and ordinary-local.

CLD v2, Proposition 7.2.8 and §7.2.11: On a locally differentially separated level-n tropical space, positive scalar-test currents correspond to unique positive Radon measures. For a middle-positive current T and a middle-positive complementary smooth form η, T∧η determines a positive Radon measure μ with ∫g dμ=⟨T,gη⟩ for compact smooth scalars g. When η has compact support, μ has compact support.

CLD v2, §§3.3.10–12 and 7.7.1–5: Ordinary smooth forms have compatible products and graded Leibniz rules. Current differentials act by graded transpose, are weakly continuous, and satisfy (d′)²=(d″)²=0, d″d′=−d′d″ and DJ=JD, where D=d′d″. In compatible degrees, ⟨DR,α⟩=⟨R,Dα⟩.
passages.quote: d′ d′′ J = J d′ d′′

passages.statement: CLD v2, §§5.8.1–5, 7.7.4, Proposition 13.3.7 and Proposition 16.6.3: On a topologically separated pure analytic space with its canonical calibration, δX=[1] is positive; on a boundaryless space it is d′- and d″-closed. Integration on a pure closed analytic subspace agrees with its associated analytic cycle current. Component coefficients retain the actual generic lengths, including nonreduced multiplicities.

CLD v2, Definitions 8.1.1 and 8.1.7: Generated Psh is the smallest ordinary subsheaf of functions valued in R∪{−∞} containing smooth positive-Hessian functions and closed under decreasing sequential limits. CPsh is the smallest ordinary subsheaf of real continuous functions containing those smooth generators and closed under uniform sequential limits.
